report_name: IDScan.net Breach Leaks 153 Million Driver's Licenses

threat_actors.name: Unnamed Cloud Intruder
threat_actors.description: The unauthorized third party responsible for breaching IDScan.net's cloud platform and exfiltrating a database of over 153 million driver's licenses, which was later put up for sale on the 'Nexus' dark web marketplace.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Cloud Storage
attack_patterns.description: An unauthorized third party gained access to IDScan.net's cloud environment and exfiltrated a database containing over 153 million U.S. and Canadian driver's licenses.

attack_patterns.name: Cloud Accounts
attack_patterns.description: The breach may have stemmed from stolen credentials for a cloud account, which would have provided the initial access needed to access the storage platform.

attack_patterns.name: Cloud Infrastructure Discovery
attack_patterns.description: The attacker likely performed discovery within the cloud environment to locate the specific storage buckets or databases containing the sensitive PII.

attack_patterns.name: Automated Exfiltration
attack_patterns.description: The exfiltration of a database containing over 153 million records suggests an automated process was used to transfer the large volume of data out of the compromised cloud storage.

identities.name: IDScan.net
identities.description: Identity verification provider that was the victim of a major data breach, resulting in the theft of a database containing over 153 million driver's licenses from its cloud platform.

identities.name: Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI)
identities.description: US law enforcement agency reportedly investigating the IDScan.net data breach.

infrastructure.name: Nexus Dark Web Marketplace
infrastructure.description: A dark web marketplace where the database stolen from IDScan.net, containing 153 million driver's licenses, was advertised for sale.

indicators.name: Anomalous Cloud Storage API Data Access
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential Cloud Storage Data Exfiltration via GetObject
id: 7c5b9f8a-1d2e-4f3c-8a9b-0e1f2a3b4c5d
status: experimental
description: Detects anomalous usage of GetObject API call, which could indicate data exfiltration from cloud storage buckets. This rule should be tuned with known good source IPs, user agents, or roles.
references:
  - https://therecord.media/idscan-data-breach-notice-drivers-licenses
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-19
tags:
  - attack.t1530
level: medium
logsource:
  product: aws
  service: cloudtrail
detection:
  selection:
    eventSource: s3.amazonaws.com
    eventName: GetObject
  filter_known_good:
    sourceIPAddress:
      - 192.0.2.1 # Placeholder for known good IPs
    userAgent:
      - KnownGoodUserAgent # Placeholder for known good user agents
  condition: selection and not filter_known_good
indicators.description: Detects anomalous API calls such as GetObject from unexpected users, roles, or IP addresses, which could indicate unauthorized data access from cloud storage.

indicators.name: Public Cloud Storage Exposure
indicators.pattern:
title: Public S3 Bucket ACL or Policy Modification
id: 8d6c0a9b-2e3f-4d5a-9b0c-1f2a3b4c5d6e
status: experimental
description: Detects when an S3 bucket's Access Control List (ACL) or bucket policy is modified to allow public access, a critical misconfiguration.
references:
  - https://therecord.media/idscan-data-breach-notice-drivers-licenses
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-19
tags:
  - attack.t1530
level: high
logsource:
  product: aws
  service: cloudtrail
detection:
  selection_put_policy:
    eventName: PutBucketPolicy
    requestParameters.bucketPolicy.Statement.Effect: 'Allow'
    requestParameters.bucketPolicy.Statement.Principal.AWS: '*'
  selection_put_acl:
    eventName: PutBucketAcl
    requestParameters.AccessControlPolicy.Grant.Grantee.URI:
      - http://acs.amazonaws.com/groups/global/AllUsers
      - http://acs.amazonaws.com/groups/global/AuthenticatedUsers
  condition: 1 of them
indicators.description: Detects configuration changes that make a cloud storage bucket publicly accessible, a common vector for data breaches.

relationships.source_name: Anomalous Cloud Storage API Data Access
